native_evaluator_audit.native_implementation: In Lean 4.33, native_decide runs evalDecideCore with native=true. +revert cleans/reverts local inputs to close the proposition; elabNativeDecideCore builds decide P, calls Lean.Meta.nativeEqTrue, then wraps the returned proof of decide P=true with of_decide_eq_true. nativeEqTrue creates a temporary Bool definition, addAndCompile compiles it, unsafe evalConst Bool evaluates it, rejects false, and inserts a fresh safe axiom asserting the returned Boolean equals true. Kernel checks the proof that uses this axiom; it does not independently enumerate P as kernel reduction.
native_evaluator_audit.observed_axiom_forms: Printed fresh examples are axiom QuantumBlockEncoding.primitiveBasisLEEquiv_six_value._native.native_decide.ax_1_1 : decide (∀ bits : PrimitiveBasis 6, exact expansion)=true and axiom QuantumBlockEncoding.splitPrimitiveWire_primitiveBits3LE_context_eq._native.native_decide.ax_1_1 : decide (∀ target : Fin 3, ∀ left right : Fin 8, exact context iff)=true. Concrete inverse examples similarly assert decide(function equality)=true.
native_evaluator_audit.fin_cases: primitiveBasisLEEquiv_two_symm uses fin_cases plus native_decide for 4 individual index cases, creating ax_1_1 through ax_1_4. primitiveBasisLEEquiv_three_symm creates 8, through ax_1_8. All other 22 native theorems create one each. Total 34 fresh native axioms.
native_evaluator_audit.finite_scopes: Six-bit universal expansion covers 64 bit assignments; each two-wire coordinate theorem ranges over 4 indices; each three-wire coordinate theorem over 8. Two-wire context iff ranges over 2*4*4=32 (target,left,right) triples and three-wire context iff over 3*8*8=192 triples. Function-equality decisions inspect finite wire/context domains; this is exhaustive finite evaluation, not sampled tests.
native_evaluator_audit.trusted_boundary: Correctness of Lean kernel/elaboration and imported proof artifacts remains necessary. Native statements additionally trust the Lean compiler/evaluator/runtime and relevant compiled arithmetic/finite-decision implementations to faithfully compute the closed Bool. This is a genuine computational axiom boundary; no hand-written domain axiom or sorryAx was reported.
native_evaluator_audit.deprecated_path: Lean.ofReduceBool and Lean.reduceBool exist but are deprecated in 4.33; the actual target proofs do NOT report them. Calling their names in a diagnostic #check only caused deprecation warnings. Their older generic trustCompiler story is not the observed proof path here.
